newsitem.title: USA: OUTLOOK - Cotton's fiber market share seen shrinking.
newsitem.headline: OUTLOOK - Cotton's fiber market share seen shrinking.

text.p: Cotton consumption should climb but its share of a growing world fiber market will shrink over the next decade, Allen Terhaar, executive director of trade promotion body Cotton Council International said.

"Asian consumer markets are widely expected to be the fastest growing fiber market for the next 10 years given current GDP (Gross Domestic Product) growth rates," he said in papers released at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's annual agricultural outlook forum.
"Unfortanately, those same Asian markets are undergoing shifts in consumption from cotton to man-made," he said.

Terhaar estimated that world cotton consumption would grow to 97.4 million bales by 2004, up from 87 million in 1996/97. Its market share was, however, seen slipping to 44.5 percent from 45.6 percent in 1996.
"I think the forecast market share may be optimistic," he said.

Terhaar said that between 1990 and 1995 polyester use grew 6.8 percent a year while cotton use barely changed. He noted several projections for the next five years placed annual growth in polyester use at seven percent while cotton increases at 1.3 percent.
The cost of production for polyester in Asian markets indicated a break-even price in the range of 40 to 55 cents per pound, or 50 to 55 cents mill-delivered in Asian markets, he said.

"There is no way that cotton can compete on a price basis with 45 cent polyester. The fact is that cotton should not even try to compete with polyester on a price basis but on a quality basis instead," Terhaar said.
Cotton Council International is the export promotion arm of the United States' National Cotton Council.
